title: Should I stay or should I show? Learning to selectively disclose information
abstract: arXiv:2609.39818v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In many high-stakes settings, human decision-makers can acquire support information before making a decision. However, acquiring information is costly, and disclosure may fail to improve human decisions or may even impair them. We tackle this problem by studying selective disclosure, i.e., the problem of learning when to reveal support information to a human decision-maker under a budget constraint. We first show that the optimal policy is a threshold rule on the Value of Information (VoI), i.e., the expected reduction in human decision risk induced by disclosure. Since VoI is unknown in practice, we estimate the regime-specific human risks and bound the possible degradation of the resulting plug-in policy relative to lack of disclosure, as well as its regret relative to the optimal policy. translated_title: 该沉默还是该展示？学习选择性地披露信息
translated_abstract: 在许多高风险决策场景中，人类决策者可以在做出决策之前获取辅助信息。然而，获取信息是有成本的，而且披露信息可能无法改善人类决策，甚至可能对其造成损害。我们通过研究选择性披露来解决这一问题，即在预算约束下学习何时向人类决策者披露辅助信息。我们首先证明了最优策略是一个基于信息价值的阈值规则，即披露所带来的对人类决策风险的预期降低。由于VoI在实践中是未知的，我们通过估计不同情形下的人类风险来构建插件策略，并界定了该策略相对于不披露时可能产生的性能退化程度，以及其相对于最优策略的遗憾值。在基准数据集上的实验表明，选择性披露的表现优于完全不披露和完全披露两种极端策略。
tldr: 该论文提出“选择性披露”问题，证明了在预算约束下最优策略是基于信息价值的阈值规则，并通过估计情形相关的人类风险构建了有理论保障的实用策略，实验表明其效果优于不披露和完全披露两种极端做法。
en_tdlr: This paper studies selective disclosure—learning when to reveal costly support information to human decision-makers under budget constraints—proving the optimal policy is a threshold rule on the Value of Information and showing the resulting plug-in policy outperforms both no disclosure and full disclosure.
